s1.syndrome_frame: Acute onset of severe low back pain and fever in a patient with chronic liver disease
salient_findings: Tenderness of the left lumbar vertebra
key_facts: Patient has chronic hepatitis B virus infection
Patient presented with weakness, bloating, anorexia, and decreased urine output for 10 days
Blood pressure on admission was 153/89 mmHg
Patient developed fever with obvious tenderness of the left lumbar vertebra
Laboratory tests showed elevated ALT and AST
Serum albumin was low at 28 g/L
Total bilirubin was elevated at 77.4 μmol/L
WBC was 3.51 × 10^9/L
Abdominal ultrasound showed liver cirrhosis and ascites
Blood culture was positive with grayish white colonies on blood agar and green colonies on TCBS agar
16S rRNA sequencing confirmed organism identity
Antibiotic susceptibility testing showed sensitivity to multiple antibiotics

shortlist.label: Spontaneous bacterial peritonitis
shortlist.why_kept: Patient has chronic hepatitis B virus infection, liver cirrhosis, and ascites, which are risk factors for spontaneous bacterial peritonitis

shortlist.label: Pyogenic spondylitis
shortlist.why_kept: Patient presented with severe low back pain and fever, which are consistent with pyogenic spondylitis

shortlist.label: Psoas abscess
shortlist.why_kept: Patient has fever, low back pain, and tenderness of the left lumbar vertebra, which are consistent with a psoas abscess

shortlist.label: Discitis
shortlist.why_kept: Patient has severe low back pain and fever, which are consistent with discitis

shortlist.label: Vibrio vulnificus infection
shortlist.why_kept: Patient has chronic hepatitis B virus infection and liver cirrhosis, which are risk factors for Vibrio vulnificus infection

raw.rationale: Patient has chronic hepatitis B virus infection, liver cirrhosis, ascites, and low serum albumin, which are risk factors for spontaneous bacterial peritonitis. The presence of a positive blood culture and abdominal ultrasound showing ascites supports this diagnosis.

rejected.label: Pyogenic spondylitis
rejected.why: Although the patient developed fever and tenderness of the left lumbar vertebra, the primary presentation and laboratory findings suggest a more systemic infection related to the liver condition.

rejected.label: Psoas abscess
rejected.why: There is no specific imaging evidence provided to support the diagnosis of a psoas abscess.

rejected.label: Discitis
rejected.why: Similar to pyogenic spondylitis, discitis would primarily present with back pain and fever, but the key findings here point towards a complication of liver disease.

rejected.label: Vibrio vulnificus infection
rejected.why: Although the blood culture showed gram-negative bacteria (suggested by growth on TCBS agar), the clinical context and the fact that Vibrio vulnificus infection is more commonly associated with exposure to contaminated water or raw seafood, which is not mentioned in the vignette.

gold: Vibrio vulnificus septicemia with underlying hepatitis B virus-associated cirrhosis
